Applying complementary slackness yields the characterization in

issues.failure_explanation: Here λ_i ≥ 0 is the multiplier of u_i ≥ 0 and μ_i ≥ 0 that of u_i ≤ C. For a minimization the correct stationarity condition is G_i − s_iρ = λ_i − μ_i. As written, at α_k = 0 (so μ_k = 0) it gives G_k − ρ = −λ_k ≤ 0, i.e. τ_k ≥ −ρ. That is the opposite of Table 1's τ_k ≤ −ρ, and every other row of the table is reversed in the same way. Table 1 is correct, but it is not derivable from the condition as stated.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the right-hand side by λ_i − μ_i, or equivalently write the Lagrangian with the correct multiplier signs.
issues.overall_effect: The stated derivation of the KKT characterization is invalid. Later sections use Table 1 directly, which is correct, so they are unaffected.
issues.title: Sign error in KKT stationarity condition; Table 1 does not follow from it
issues.why_classification: A local sign fix restores consistency, and every downstream claim already rests on the correct table.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the KKT conditions still bound $-\rho$ from
A descent direction exists if and only if $\tau_i > \tau_j$.

issues.failure_explanation: By Table 1, at optimality every i in Iup has τ_i ≤ −ρ and every j in Idown has τ_j ≥ −ρ. Hence max_Iup τ = τ_{i*} ≤ −ρ ≤ τ_{j*} = min_Idown τ, consistent with Δ ≤ 0 at an optimum. The display asserts the opposite, which is impossible whenever Δ < 0 at convergence. The shrinking section makes the same misreading when it claims, 'from (mvp) and Table', that the optimal −ρ lies in [τ_{j*}, τ_{i*}] at a non-optimal iterate. Table 1 describes the optimum only and does not support that claim.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reverse the inequality to τ_{i*} ≤ −ρ ≤ τ_{j*} at optimality. Present the shrinking interval as a heuristic rather than a consequence of Table 1.
issues.overall_effect: The stated KKT bracket for b is wrong. The midpoint estimator is unaffected because it is symmetric. The justification of the shrinking thresholds is unsupported.
issues.title: Reversed KKT bounds on the threshold −ρ
issues.why_classification: A local correction suffices; the bias estimate, the algorithm and the guarantees are unchanged.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Free variables ($0 < u_i < C_{k(i)}$) are never frozen.

issues.failure_explanation:
Freezing acts on a training point, removing both α_k and α_k*, but criteria (s1)–(s4) are per variable. Two problems follow:
- When α_k = α_k* = 0, both (s1) and (s3) apply and may disagree, so 'the applicable criterion' is undefined.
- When one variable is at a bound and the other is free (e.g. α_k = 0, α_k* free), (s1) can be met. Then k is frozen together with a free variable, contradicting the stated rule.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Freeze k only if neither of its variables is free and every bound variable of k meets its own criterion, or shrink at the level of individual variables.
issues.overall_effect: The active-set procedure is ambiguous and can freeze KKT-relevant variables. This causes premature inner termination and extra unshrinking cycles. The final reconstruction check still guards correctness.
issues.title: Per-training-point shrinking rule is ill-defined and can freeze free variables
issues.why_classification: A routine specification fix; correctness is protected by unshrinking and no guarantee changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The only loop is the for-loop over t, which has already exited, so 'continue outer loop' has no target. Control flow after unshrinking is undefined. An exit caused by reaching maxiter without Δ ≤ tol is not distinguished from convergence. The algorithm may therefore return an uncertified iterate, or re-loop with no iteration bound. The midpoint fallback uses i* and j* selected over the shrunk set before reconstruction, not the full-set extremizers from (full-violation).
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Wrap the loop in an outer repeat-until with a global iteration budget. Recompute i* and j* over the full sets after reconstruction. Report non-convergence when the budget is exhausted.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the algorithm does not deliver its contract of a certified ε_tol-optimal (α, α*, b).
issues.title: Unshrinking branch jumps to a nonexistent outer loop; termination and final bias underspecified
issues.why_classification: A standard control-flow fix restores the intended procedure with no change to the method or its guarantees.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: need not be positive semi-definite, so $\eta_s < 0$ is possible.
For $a = -1$, $\Omega_s$ may fail to be positive
symmetric-kernel variant~(m2, Section~\ref{sec:m2}), $\eta$ may be negative

issues.failure_explanation:
Ω* is a cross-kernel matrix, not a Gram matrix. For the RBF kernel with x_2 = −x_1 ≠ 0, Ω* = [[e^{−4γ‖x_1‖²}, 1], [1, e^{−4γ‖x_1‖²}]] has negative determinant. The premise is therefore false, and the a = +1 PSD and convergence claim is unsupported as argued.

The valid argument assumes K(−x,−x′) = K(x,x′), which holds for RBF. It writes K(x,x′) + aK(x,−x′) = ½⟨φ(x)+aφ(−x), φ(x′)+aφ(−x′)⟩, which is PSD for both a = ±1. So the claims that a = −1 (with RBF) can give η_s < 0, needs a fallback, and falls outside the convergence proof are also wrong. Without this invariance, Ω_s need not even be symmetric for either sign.

failure_location.quote: follows from the fact that $\Omega$ and $\Omega^*$ are individually PSD.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Assume a symmetric kernel with K(−x,−x′) = K(x,x′). Prove Ω_s ⪰ 0 for both signs via the feature map φ(x) + aφ(−x). Extend the convergence statement to a = −1 and drop the claims of negative curvature.
issues.overall_effect: The m2 convergence guarantee for a = +1 rests on a false premise. The statements excluding a = −1 from the guarantees and requiring the negative-curvature fallback are incorrect.
issues.title: Incorrect PSD analysis of the symmetric kernel matrix Ω_s
issues.why_classification: It needs a replacement argument plus an added kernel condition, and several m2 statements must be revised. The core results survive, and are in fact strengthened.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: Rewriting criteria~\eqref{eq:s3} and~\eqref{eq:s4} in terms of $\tau_k$
yielding a smaller effective active set and
The asymmetry in Lemma~\ref{lem:asymmetry} is the direct consequence of
heuristic adapted to the sample-dependent bounds is derived and shown to

issues.failure_explanation:
The paper claims that the shrinking asymmetry yields smaller active sets and practical convergence acceleration. Lemma lem:asymmetry only re-expresses (s3)–(s4) through the identity τ_{N+k} = τ_k + 2y_kε/100. The tests on α_k* still act on the variable's own score τ_{N+k} and have exactly the standard SMO form, so the set of frozen variables is unchanged; nothing about active-set size or speed follows.

The gap comes from the ε-tube term in q, not from the sample-dependent bounds. Standard ε-SVR has the same asymmetry with gap 2ε. No analysis or experiment in the source supports the acceleration claim.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Withdraw the claim or state it as a conjecture, and attribute the gap to the tube term. Alternatively, supply empirical or analytical evidence of acceleration.
issues.overall_effect: The advertised practical benefit of the MAPE-adapted shrinking, in the abstract, computational remarks and conclusion, is unsupported.
issues.title: Unsupported claim that the MAPE-induced shrinking asymmetry accelerates convergence
issues.why_classification: The repair withdraws an advertised contribution, but the formal algorithmic results are unaffected.
